bodyParagraphs: NASA's November 19 report describes flowers in Chile's Atacama Desert during spring 2026. Earlier rain helped dormant seeds wake and begin growing in the soil. The desert is normally one of the driest places on Earth. Landsat satellites recorded the landscape in September and October, showing the flowering season from space. Landsat 8 recorded the September view, while Landsat 9 supplied the October view. The November report looks back at the flowering seen in these September and October images. These observations show the colorful change in a normally dry desert landscape.

bodyParagraphs: NASA's astronomy feature for November 19 presents the Horsehead and Flame Nebulas. The Horsehead is a cloud of dust and gas with a shape that resembles a horse's head. The feature describes it as about five light-years tall and approximately 1,500 light-years away. These figures describe its size and distance, respectively. The dark horse-like form gives the object its familiar name. NASA presents the Horsehead together with the Flame Nebula in the same astronomy feature. This is a daily presentation of these objects, with the Horsehead's shape, material and distance explained for readers.

bodyParagraphs: UNESCO and CodeAI have scheduled an online workshop for teachers on November 19, 2026. It is aimed at teachers and education professionals in Latin America and the Caribbean. Participants are to try AI for Oceans, an activity using pictures of fish and marine waste. They will classify these images to explore how a machine learning model uses data. The exercise is also intended to reveal potential errors and biases in the system's decisions. No previous programming knowledge is required. UNESCO describes the session as a hands-on opportunity to learn about AI and consider its use in teaching.
